text:
amy: Heads-up — between 15:12-15:18 UTC we saw a serious tail-latency spike for model ‘redwood-xl-6B-q4’ during a traffic burst. P50 ~ 40ms (ok) but P99 jumped to ~1.2s and a few requests hit 2.3s. Autoscaler did not refill warm pool fast enough; saw several cold-start allocations. :rotating_light:
ben: Seeing the same on traces. Root cause looks correlated with kernel-selection fallback on two nodes — logs show fallback to slower matmul kernel at batch sizes ~8-12. Also noticed KV cache misses spiking ~6x during the window.
carla: Posting snippets: infra-bot reported provision events and kernel fallback logs —
carla: ```
[15:13:02] kernel_selector: selected=fast_gemm_v2 for seq_len=256 batch=4
[15:13:05] kernel_selector: fallback=generic_gemm for seq_len=128 batch=10 reason="tile_mismatch"
[15:13:06] kv_cache: miss_rate=0.72 -> 0.78
[15:13:06] warm_pool: lease_returned=3 free=1 target=6
```
dave: Interesting — batch distribution histogram shows a shift toward medium batches (8-12) because a new client started sending multi-turn parallel requests. Our kernel guardrails assume small batches or large batches; medium batches are hitting unoptimized path.
eric: Also saw GPU utilization spike on two machines while neighbors were idle, pointing to noisy neighbor scheduling / placement imbalance. One host was running a long-running fusion job from a test cluster (noisy), which likely reduced available tensor cores and pushed kernel selector into fallback.
amy: TL;DR: three contributing things: kernel-selection fallback for medium batch sizes, KV cache miss storm (prefix mismatch + cold cache), and slow warm-pool replenishment (scale policy + provisioning jitter).
ben: Quick profiling from 15:13:10 — attach flame summary (abbrev):
ben: ```
runtime_kernel_time: 78% (fallback kernels)
kv_lookup: 9% (increased misses)
batching_overhead: 6% (queue latency)
network_attach: 4%
```
carla: We also have evict logs showing aggressive KV eviction due to memory pressure around 15:12:50, which explains miss spike. Memory pressure came from a mis-sized model shard pinned by that noisy neighbor job.
dave: Immediate mitigations proposed: 1) Temporary increase warm_pool target by +4 for the affected pools, 2) pin kernel-selection to prefer known-good gemm for medium batches (feature flag), 3) throttle the offending client via rate-limit rule, 4) evict/test the noisy neighbor workload. Thoughts?
amy: Agree. Add 5) increase KV prefetch window for mult-turn to reduce misses during bursts.
eric: I can trigger a one-off warm pool scale and kill the noisy neighbor job on the infra side. Ben can flip the kernel-selection flag?
ben: I can. I'll push kernel-selection guardrail flag to prefer fast_gemm_v2 for batch sizes 6-16 as a short-term fix. Will monitor regression risk.
carla: I'll increase warm_pool target for the pools serving that model in eu-west-1 by +4 and temporarily relax the autoscaler cooldown.
dave: I'll open a quick client-rate-limit rule in API gateway and coordinate with growth to throttle the multi-turn test client.
amy: After immediate mitigations, can we run a focused perf test (staging) with synthetic medium-batch workload to validate kernel selector heuristics and confirm no quality regressions?
ben: Yes — I'll orchestrate a canary run with kernel flag on a small fleet. If stable, we'll bake heuristics into kernel selector and add a unit to the kernel cost model for medium batch performance.
eric: Infra notes: provisioning jitter traced to a slow nvlink init on two GPUs (driver handshake east region). I'll file a follow-up with drivers team and add a health-check patch.
carla: Logging next steps + owners in Incident doc. Schedule 30m scrub @ 16:00 UTC to triage longer term: tuning batching heuristics, KV prefetch defaults, kernel cost model updates, and autoscaler scale-up latency SLOs.
amy: Thanks all. Marking thread resolved when warm pool + kernel flag are live and P99 < 400ms for 10m. (reacts :white_check_mark:)
